title: MADBench: Benchmarking the Security of Multi-Agent Debate
abstract: arXiv:2609.39146v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-agent debate (MAD) can improve large language model (LLM) reasoning by allowing multiple agents to exchange and critique their answers to the same task. However, the interactions that enable agents to correct mistakes can also spread adversarial errors and steer the agents toward an incorrect answer. Although some efforts have been made to examine particular attack types on MAD, systematic evaluation of MAD under diverse attacks remains limited. A central question is whether debate mitigates adversarial influence or amplifies it.   In this paper, we present MADBench, a benchmark for evaluating the security of MAD. We organize attacks into a layered taxonomy following the MAD workflow, incorporating both established attacks and new strategies tailored to debate. translated_title: MADBench：多智能体辩论安全性基准测试
translated_abstract: 多智能体辩论（MAD）通过让多个智能体就同一任务交换并批判彼此的答案，可以提升大语言模型（LLM）的推理能力。然而，这些使智能体能够纠正错误的交互，也可能传播对抗性错误，并将智能体引向错误答案。尽管已有一些工作研究了针对MAD的特定攻击类型，但在多样化攻击下对MAD的系统性评估仍然有限。一个核心问题是：辩论究竟是缓解了对抗性影响，还是放大了它。本文提出了MADBench，一个用于评估多智能体辩论安全性的基准。我们按照MAD工作流程将攻击组织成分层分类体系，既纳入了已有的攻击，也包含了专为辩论场景设计的新策略。我们在356个源任务和3,958个测试用例上评估了六类攻击族，考察它们对最终答案的影响以及对抗性影响的传播。
tldr: 该论文提出MADBench——一个系统评估多智能体辩论安全性的基准，通过涵盖六类攻击族、356个源任务和3,958个测试用例的分层攻击分类体系，考察对抗攻击对最终答案的影响及对抗性影响的传播。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MADBench, a benchmark for systematically evaluating the security of multi-agent debate, organizing attacks into a layered taxonomy across six attack families, 356 source tasks, and 3,958 test cases to assess their effects on final answers and the propagation of adversarial influence.
